clue.text: Invited one to keep quiet — one most voluble

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it inside, so the guest's letters go round the rest

parts.note: someone invited is a guest
SH is the call for quiet
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A guest is asked to hush, being the chattiest person at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invited one' reads as an adjective phrase but is a noun for a guest; 'to keep' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of gushy: effusive talk pouring out, the most talkative of all.

clue.text: Possible US version of Morse to stick with Oxford?

parts.note: to gum is to stick together
an Oxford is a style of laced shoe

explanation.surface: An American adaptation of Inspector Morse would stay faithful to its Oxford setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the fictional detective set in Oxford; here Oxford is a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a detective, and Morse is a famous fictional detective.

clue.text: Blue, ornately gabled storage place for bicycles

parts.note: blue means sad, low in spirits

indicators.note: ornately suggests the letters of gabled are dressed up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sad scene: an ornate gabled shed for storing bikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch hung from a bike's carrier holds luggage, so it is storage on a bicycle.

clue.text: Element in certain form -very first to fill in that is

indicators.note: the very and first pieces fill the gap in the that is piece

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
top means first, best

explanation.surface: Instructions for filling in a form, putting things first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is a variant of an element, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant of a chemical element differing in neutron count: the element in one particular form.

clue.text: Safe at the outset, except if dark

indicators.note: at the outset means just the first letter of Safe

parts.note: unless means except if

explanation.surface: You're safe to start with, except when it's dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Without daylight, so lacking light: a synonym for dark.

clue.text: Age added to small passport, perhaps — in profile?

indicators.note: the age is tacked on after the other pieces

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a passport is an example of ID, identification
an eon is a vast age

explanation.surface: A traveller's passport photo gets an age stamp beside it, and the picture is taken from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the passport as just one kind of ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from the side, as a face in profile is viewed: a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Girl from Parma, maybe, briefly passing by in it

indicators.note: the shortened passing-by word goes inside the it piece

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: ignoring someone is passing them by

explanation.surface: A girl from Parma walks past briefly with some sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal; 'briefly' drops the final letter, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for an unmarried young woman, so a girl from an Italian city such as Parma.

clue.text: Follow press chief's self-introduction, lifting issue of Mercury?

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to dog is to follow
an editor, ED, introducing himself says I'm Ed

explanation.surface: A press chief introduces himself and follows up a story while raising an issue of a newspaper called Mercury.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury is a god, and 'issue' is offspring, not an edition of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A child of a god and a mortal, half divine: the offspring of a god such as Mercury.

clue.text: Ex-pupil with something painted blue

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
a scene is something an artist paints

explanation.surface: A former student paints a picture in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' means smutty, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of indecent or smutty, as blue jokes are.

clue.text: Around ten or eleven Deutschmarks men acquire digging around

indicators.note: the digging goes around the other pieces, which it acquires inside itself

parts.note: mining is digging for ore
DM is the abbreviation for Deutschmarks, the old German currency
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers: men

explanation.surface: German money and workmen seem caught up in an excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquire' tells us DM and OR are taken into MINING. OR stands for 'other ranks', ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A time partway through the morning, the coffee-break hours of ten or eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Husky command perhaps features mawkishness

definitions.meaning: the shout a sled driver gives to start the dogs running

explanation.surface: A sled dog's orders turn out to be sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: Husky is the sled dog, not a gruff voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The driver's cry to a dog team, and also a word for sloppy sentiment: two senses.

clue.text: Keep mum's old house on — get name off the wall

indicators.note: something off the wall is crazy, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wants to hang on to their mother's old home and take a sign down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep mum' is an idiom for staying silent, not caring for a mother; 'off the wall' rearranges OLD HOUSE ON GET plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to stay silent and say nothing, as mum means quiet.

clue.text: Returned unfinished perfume and note enclosing book tokens

indicators.note: returned means the assembled letters are read backwards
the perfume and note together wrap round the book
the last letter of the perfume word is cut off

parts.note: perfume is a smell
ME is a variant of MI, the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a half-used scent with a note and some book tokens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final L; ME is a variant spelling of the sol-fa note MI, and 'Returned' turns the whole run round.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbols that stand for something, as badges and tokens do: synonyms.

clue.text: Pillar and beam, the first falling on pitch

indicators.note: the first letter falls lower, to the bottom of the word in this down clue

parts.note: to beam is to smile
pitch is musical tone

explanation.surface: A pillar and a beam collapse onto a pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' is a smile, not a girder; 'the first falling' sends S to the end, making MILES.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside stone post marking distance, a kind of pillar.

clue.text: Watches film, thinking normally

parts.note: to watch is to mind, as in minding the children
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Someone watching a film is lost in thought, as people usually are.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual attitude, one's usual way of thinking about things.

clue.text: Host with piece of cake and cocktail

parts.note: a host means a great number, as does a sea of faces
something easy is a piece of cake, or a breeze

explanation.surface: A party host serves cake with drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' is a multitude, not someone entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A vodka, cranberry and grapefruit drink is a named cocktail.

clue.text: For one grand render flat fare

parts.note: e.g., for example, is 'for one'
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
to roll dough or a lawn is to flatten it

explanation.surface: Someone pays a thousand to have things flattened, a costly fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' means food, not the price of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese takeaway snack, a stuffed fried pancake, is an example of fare in the sense of food.

clue.text: Achieve influence in dispute

parts.note: to gain is to achieve
to have a say is to have influence

explanation.surface: Someone gets their way in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny or contradict, which is to dispute a claim.

clue.text: Do take over from others, nothing having been arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone takes over from colleagues because nothing was organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a film take, not seizing control.
explanation.definitionFit: To film a scene again is to do another take.

clue.text: California bishops prepared with special scripture reading

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for two
in cookery, à la means prepared in the style of

explanation.surface: Californian clergy get ready to read special scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jewish mystical tradition interpreting scripture by hidden meanings: an esoteric reading of holy text.

clue.text: City solid, preserving record

indicators.note: preserving means the solid shape keeps the record safe inside it

parts.note: a cone is a geometric solid
a log is a record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A city's firm commitment to keeping its records.
explanation.definitionFit: A German city on the Rhine, Köln.

clue.text: Buckle on clobber, raised decorative fastening

parts.note: to buckle is to bow, bend under weight

indicators.note: raised means read upwards in this down clue, so backwards

parts.note: to tonk is to hit hard, to clobber

explanation.surface: A buckle on a clothing item is a raised decoration fastening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' looks like British slang for clothes, but here it is a verb, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental tie with loops, a decorative way of fastening.

clue.text: Did tea menu in the end, surprisingly not cooked?

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order
in the end means the last letter of menu

explanation.surface: Someone had tea from a menu but the food came out raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' means falsified, as books are cooked; accounts that have been checked are presumably honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts officially examined are verified, so the books have not been cooked or fiddled.

clue.text: Fancy meeting point ultimately is like arcade with globe outside

indicators.note: the other pieces sit outside the single final letter, which goes in between them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of the word point

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as gold'
a shopping arcade is a mall
the globe is the world

explanation.surface: A meeting point that's like a shopping arcade, with the whole globe outside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T, which goes inside IS to make ITS. 'Fancy meeting' is the start of 'Fancy meeting you here!', not an attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of surprise at bumping into an acquaintance far from home, as fancy meeting you here.

clue.text: Location visited on and off or seldom

indicators.note: visiting on and off means taking every other letter of the words or seldom

explanation.surface: A place one goes to only now and then, or hardly ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital is an example of a location, a place.

clue.text: Arguably, bovine fellow needs hospital department to supply this?

definitions.text: Arguably, bovine fellow needs hospital department to supply this?

parts.note: oxy could arguably be an adjective meaning like an ox, i.e. bovine
a gent is a fellow
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A cow-like man needs a hospital department to supply him with something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a hospital department supplies this to a patient struggling to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy over a hospital bed into which breathing gas is fed for the patient.

clue.text: Maybe miss visiting hotel? Try motel after a spin

indicators.note: after a spin the letters picked out are read backwards
visiting means the letters are found inside the words hotel? Try motel

explanation.surface: A young woman, perhaps, is staying at a hotel and thinks about trying a motel after a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so an example of a miss, a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Idiot heard to run into van

indicators.note: heard means the spoken sound of the run-into word is used

parts.note: to run into someone is to meet them
the van, short for vanguard, is the head of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A fool is said to have crashed into a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is the vanguard, the front, not a vehicle; 'heard' gives the spelling MEAT for MEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a stupid person, a dimwit or blockhead.
